title: Paul Before the Sanhedrin, The Plot Against Paul, Transfer to Caesarea

questions.question: Paul looked intently at the council and said "Brothers, I have lived my life before God in all good conscience up to this day." The high priest Ananias commanded those near Paul to do what?
options: Strike him on the mouth
Remove him from the council chamber
Bind him with chains again immediately
Stand him aside while the elders deliberated
questions.explanation: Acts 23:2 (ESV): "And the high priest Ananias commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth."

questions.question: Paul unknowingly reviled the high priest, calling him a "whitewashed wall." When he was told the man was the high priest, what did Paul say?
options: "I did not know, brothers, that he was the high priest, for it is written, 'You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.'"
"Forgive me; I spoke in anger and not with the Spirit's guidance."
"Then I retract my words and ask forgiveness before this council."
"I will speak more carefully, though his action was unjust."
questions.correctAnswer: "I did not know, brothers, that he was the high priest, for it is written, 'You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.'"
questions.explanation: Acts 23:5 (ESV): "Paul said, 'I did not know, brothers, that he was the high priest, for it is written, 'You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.'"

questions.question: Paul perceived that some were Sadducees and others Pharisees. He cried out "Brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. It is with respect to the hope and the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial." What was the effect of this?
options: A dissension arose between the Pharisees and the Sadducees and the assembly was divided
The Pharisees defended him and the Sadducees demanded immediate execution
The council erupted into chaos and the tribune had to intervene at once
Both Pharisees and Sadducees argued that Paul's trial was invalid
questions.correctAnswer: A dissension arose between the Pharisees and the Sadducees and the assembly was divided
questions.explanation: Acts 23:7 (ESV): "And when he had said this, a dissension arose between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the assembly was divided."

questions.question: What is the key theological difference the text states the Sadducees held versus the Pharisees?
options: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all
The Sadducees rejected the oral law while Pharisees embraced it
The Sadducees believed in predestination while Pharisees in free will
The Sadducees denied the messiah while Pharisees awaited him eagerly
questions.correctAnswer: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all
questions.explanation: Acts 23:8 (ESV): "For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all."

questions.question: That night the Lord stood by Paul and said: "Take courage, for as you have testified to the facts about me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in..."?
options: Rome
Greece
Asia
Caesarea
questions.explanation: Acts 23:11 (ESV): "The following night the Lord stood by him and said, 'Take courage, for as you have testified to the facts about me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome.'"

questions.question: More than forty Jews bound themselves under an oath neither to eat nor drink until they had done what?
options: Killed Paul
Obtained Paul's release
Brought Paul before the high priest again
Expelled Paul from Jerusalem permanently
questions.explanation: Acts 23:12-13 (ESV): "When it was day, the Jews made a plot and bound themselves by an oath neither to eat nor drink till they had killed Paul. There were more than forty who made this conspiracy."

questions.question: Who discovered the plot and warned Paul?
options: The son of Paul's sister
A believing centurion who overheard the plan
Lydia's husband who had contacts in Jerusalem
A Pharisee on the council who sympathized with Paul
questions.explanation: Acts 23:16 (ESV): "Now the son of Paul's sister heard of their ambush, so he went and entered the barracks and told Paul."

questions.question: The tribune Claudius Lysias arranged a large escort to take Paul safely to Caesarea. How many soldiers accompanied Paul?
options: Two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen
One hundred soldiers and fifty horsemen as a guard
Four centurions with fifty soldiers each and a cavalry escort
Five hundred soldiers of the garrison and all available horses
questions.correctAnswer: Two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen
questions.explanation: Acts 23:23 (ESV): "Then he called two of the centurions and said, 'Get ready two hundred soldiers, with seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen to go as far as Caesarea at the third hour of the night.'"

questions.question: The tribune wrote a letter to Governor Felix about Paul. What was his overall assessment of Paul's case?
options: I found that he was being accused about questions of their law, but charged with nothing deserving death or imprisonment
Paul appeared to be a dangerous agitator who should remain in custody
The case was complex and required the wisdom of the governor to decide
Paul had committed no clear crime against Roman law or the Jewish temple
questions.correctAnswer: I found that he was being accused about questions of their law, but charged with nothing deserving death or imprisonment
questions.explanation: Acts 23:29 (ESV): "I found that he was being accused about questions of their law, but charged with nothing deserving death or imprisonment."

questions.question: Governor Felix read the letter and asked Paul what province he was from. When he learned Paul was from Cilicia he said he would hear Paul's case when the accusers arrived. Where did he order Paul to be kept?
options: In Herod's praetorium (palace/headquarters)
In the common prison of Caesarea
Under house arrest in a private home
In the custody of a centurion at the barracks
questions.explanation: Acts 23:35 (ESV): "he said, 'I will give you a hearing when your accusers arrive.' And he commanded him to be guarded in Herod's praetorium."

questions.question: Some Pharisees spoke up on Paul's behalf in the Sanhedrin. What did they say?
options: "We find nothing wrong in this man. What if a spirit or an angel spoke to him?"
"This man is a Pharisee and has done nothing worthy of death."
"His teaching about the resurrection is fully in accord with our tradition."
"Let us not oppose him lest we be found fighting against God."
questions.correctAnswer: "We find nothing wrong in this man. What if a spirit or an angel spoke to him?"
questions.explanation: Acts 23:9 (ESV): "Then some of the scribes of the Pharisees' party stood up and contended sharply, 'We find nothing wrong in this man. What if a spirit or an angel spoke to him?'"

questions.question: Paul called the high priest Ananias a "whitewashed wall." This was because Ananias commanded Paul to be struck. What did Paul predict would happen to the high priest?
options: "God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall!"
"Your injustice will be repaid before God on the last day."
"You sit to judge me by the law, yet you yourself break it."
"The God of our fathers will not honor your priesthood."
questions.correctAnswer: "God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall!"
questions.explanation: Acts 23:3 (ESV): "Then Paul said to him, 'God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall! Are you sitting to judge me according to the law, and yet contrary to the law you order me to be struck?'"

questions.question: Paul told the tribune who conveyed his nephew's news about the plot: "Tell no one that you have informed me of this." This shows Paul's concern for what?
options: His nephew's safety from those who made the oath
Keeping the tribune unaware of the informant's identity
Preventing the plotters from changing their plan
Protecting the Pharisees on the council who had supported him
questions.correctAnswer: His nephew's safety from those who made the oath
questions.explanation: Acts 23:22 (ESV): "So the tribune dismissed the young man, charging him, 'Tell no one that you have informed me of these things.'" Paul's words (v.19) showed concern for the boy's safety.

questions.question: The tribune's name, revealed in his letter to Felix, was what?
options: Claudius Lysias
Julius Maximus
Cornelius Felix
Antonius Marcellus
questions.explanation: Acts 23:26 (ESV): "Claudius Lysias, to his Excellency the governor Felix, greetings."

questions.question: How were the soldiers ordered to travel — by night or by day?
options: They set out at night, leaving at the third hour of the night
They traveled by day to deter an ambush in the open road
They left at dawn with a full military escort
They departed at noon to reach Antipatris before dark
questions.correctAnswer: They set out at night, leaving at the third hour of the night
questions.explanation: Acts 23:23 (ESV): "Get ready two hundred soldiers, with seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen to go as far as Caesarea at the third hour of the night."

key_verse_text: "Take courage, for as you have testified to the facts about me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome."
